name: g2-i1-vs-i1-stagmem-maxfeat-none-v1
question: Does adding only target-stagger memory reproduce the improvement in stagger_punish and the losses in reflex and face_first observed with the full I2-memory feature set?
nature: Follow-up diagnostic motivated by previously seen results (I1 vs I2-memory, reflex audit, conditional reflex audit). Not a blind evaluation; val/test/shift results of related models were already seen. Not a causal test of individual features. No statement about game performance.

splits.note: assignments from the manifest @6ccafc0, unchanged; pending (22 scenes, 20261012_215634_burg-upper) excluded; no val-based selection, no dirty-run retraining, one seed

conditions.A_I1: I1-current: rf_i1current.features + rf_i1current.Encoder fitted on train (unchanged, 61 columns)
conditions.B_I1_stagmem: A's 61 columns unchanged and in the same order, then the 6 stagger-memory columns appended at the end (spec: memory_features)

memory_features.source: Fight attributes _stag_ptr / _stag_t, written only by souls/duel.py prep_reflex (4th entry of RULES): if T.a in STAGGER: if F._stag_ptr != F.ptr: F._stag_ptr, F._stag_t = F.ptr, T.now; else: F._stag_ptr = None (_stag_t is left as is). Introduced in 93dce7b (P-80); identical in all 18 post-P-80 run commits of the manifest.
memory_features.capture_timing: scenes.capture runs before RULES (duel loop: SCENE_TAP.tick before 'for rule in RULES'), so the captured values are the state left by the latest earlier prep_reflex call in this Fight (previous tick that reached rule 4), never the update of this tick. Fight is created per duel() call, so the attributes do not exist until the first prep_reflex of that fight.
memory_features.time_convention: T.now = time.time() in _sense; scenes._plain stores a float > 1e9 as {'_t': v - T.now} with the same T.now as this tick. elapsed = -_t seconds.

primitives.name: smem_active
primitives.meaning: an active stagger streak was remembered at the latest prep_reflex
primitives.value: 1.0 if fight._stag_ptr is not None; 0.0 if key present and None
primitives.missing: key _stag_ptr absent (not recorded: code before 93dce7b, or no prep_reflex yet in this fight) -> NaN + smem_active__missing=1

primitives.name: smem_is_target
primitives.meaning: the remembered staggered entity is the current target
primitives.value: 1.0 if fight._stag_ptr == tick.ptr; 0.0 if _stag_ptr is not None and != tick.ptr
primitives.missing: no active memory (key absent or None) -> NaN + smem_is_target__missing=1

primitives.name: smem_target_since_s
primitives.meaning: seconds since the remembered stagger streak of the current target began (first prep_reflex that saw it in STAGGER)
primitives.value: -fight._stag_t._t, only if fight._stag_ptr == tick.ptr and _stag_t is a {'_t'} timer
primitives.missing: any other case -> NaN + smem_target_since_s__missing=1 (in particular a _stag_t left over while _stag_ptr is None, or one belonging to another ptr, is never used)

memory_features.fitted_statistics: none (no scaling, no vocabulary); NaN stays NaN in the value column as in the I1 encoder
memory_features.not_inputs: raw pointers (_stag_ptr, tick.ptr) are compared for equality only; absolute times, coordinates, ids are not inputs
caveats: missingness of smem_active is mostly a code-version marker (train: 592 of 601 'key absent' scenes come from runs before 93dce7b)
the streak start is the first prep_reflex that saw the stagger, not the game's stagger onset (tick granularity; ticks that end before rule 4 do not update)
a stagger that ends and restarts between two prep_reflex calls is seen as one streak
when the target becomes staggered this tick the memory is still None/absent; the current anim is already in I1 (tgt_anim, tgt_anim_cat)
dirty run commits (uncommitted changes) cannot be checked against the code

excluded_inputs: all other fight timers and counters
style, flags, weapon name, nm/map id, ground, arena
run, scene_seq, commit, split, fight id (audit metadata only)
rule, out, future observations, hits, outcomes, ctl links

model.max_features_note: max_features=None (all columns considered at each split) is a NEW diagnostic setting, not the C3 setting (C3 used 'sqrt'). Both A and B are trained with it; the preserved C3 predictions (sqrt) cannot stand in for A; historical C3/C4 results are not replaced. Considering all features does not isolate the information value of memory or establish causality (bootstrap and tie-breaking still random).

overall: macro F1 over the preserved primary class set (baseline results A_base lookup primary_classes per split)
macro F1 over all true classes present in the split
exact label lists for each macro F1
per class P/R/F1, true n, predicted n, supporting runs
per-run accuracy and its unweighted mean

core_condition.definition: same as conditional_reflex_audit.py cond(): A = tick.a in range(3500,3600); B = some snap.chars entry with ptr != tick.ptr, team in {6,7,24,25,27,33}, hp > 0, anim in range(3000,3500), horizontal distance to player < 2.5 m; core = A and B
core_condition.report: per split and pooled (supplementary): scene n, run n, A/B correct counts, recall (null when n=0), paired groups

interpretation.tradeoff: stagger_punish improves while reflex or face_first worsens -> 'the small memory set reproduces the same directional trade-off'
interpretation.one_sided: only improvements or only losses -> report them, do not attribute the full I2 result to these features
interpretation.little_change: -> 'this configuration did not reproduce the pattern'; do not conclude memory is irrelevant

boundary: stage 'prepare' builds and checks matrices only (fit/predict are patched to raise); stage 'train' needs --approved TRAINING-APPROVED and is not run during preparation
